scope: Public-source evidence review of 13 existing country-system records; original coding was produced collaboratively.
status: All 64 review proposals remained unapplied as of 6 November 2026; publishing this archive does not change shared research data.
limits: Manufacturer specifications are attributed claims, not independent performance tests.
A source checked only through indexed text is labeled in its location field.
Unknown means not established by the sources reviewed, not proven absence.
Original shared-workbook contents, collaborator entries and private document identifiers are omitted.
The 7 November consolidation corrects one exact-date overstatement: Lithuania’s first shipment had arrived by its 7 October announcement; exact arrival day was not established.

reviews.finding: SkyStriker citations are mixed with Orbiter sources. The $105,000 estimate is traceable, but AI/ML is not established.
reviews.evidence_note: Azerbaijan had SkyStriker by January 2019; September exercise reporting described Army service. These observations do not establish exact first delivery or operational acceptance. The 2023 USD 105,000 price is a generic published estimate, not Azerbaijan’s paid price. The reported 100 km is not explicitly total flight distance. Elbit’s endurance depends on payload. Commercial aviation activity through Universal Avionics is documented, but shared civilian technology is unresolved. Tracking and autonomous navigation alone do not establish AI/ML. Annual production capacity is unknown.

reviews.finding: The 2020 receipt year conflicts with official evidence of possession in 2018. The product URL now redirects to a different model.
reviews.evidence_note: An official June 2018 parade account names Orbiter 1K, establishing possession before 2020. First receipt and first operational fielding remain unknown; a parade or an inventory estimate does not date either event. FlightGlobal reported licensed Azad Systems production in 2017. The historical 1K brochure is the appropriate specification source; the former product link now redirects to Orbiter 2 LM. Its 50 km is mission range, not explicitly total flight distance. Published price estimates are generic. Zarba-related names need configuration matching; do not merge them automatically. AI use, commercial products and annual production capacity remain unverified.

reviews.finding: Reported Pakistani use in 2025 is supported. The local joint-production arrangement does not settle import status. Later Sivrisinek AI claims do not establish the 2025 configuration.
reviews.evidence_note: Reuters reported Pakistani use in May 2025 and local assembly through Baykar and NASTP. The checked sources do not establish a foreign purchase, licence or first import date. Reported range and payload figures are attributed to an Indian Army display of a recovered unit, not independent manufacturer confirmation. Current Sivrisinek AI claims cannot be assumed for Pakistan’s 2025 configuration. Baykar’s completed Piaggio acquisition supports commercial aircraft activity, but related civilian technology remains unresolved. Price, endurance and annual capacity were not established. An unknown price leaves price-based inclusion unresolved.

reviews.finding: Service by 2026 is reported from Serb at the exhibition. A formal introduction date is not established. Computer-assisted tracking does not prove AI.
reviews.evidence_note: Exhibition reporting attributes service by 2026 to Serb; the actual introduction date could be earlier. Janes reported production in 2024 but did not date Jaser deliveries. Its separate Samil discussion must not supply Jaser’s datalink or delivery claims. Computer-assisted tracking does not establish AI/ML. Reported effective range is not explicitly flight distance. Exports, commercial products, annual capacity and unit price remain unverified. Small size does not establish a price threshold.

reviews.finding: The UAE order is confirmed. Operational fielding and unit price remain unverified. Exact-model manufacturer material supports AI. The 50 km figure is communication range.
reviews.evidence_note: EDGE announced a UAE order covering Hunter 2-S, Hunter 5 and Hunter 10 on 21 February 2023. It does not establish completed delivery or operational acceptance. The AED 1.1 billion package lacks model quantities, so it cannot establish a unit price. The Hunter 2-S datasheet labels 50 km as communication range. It explicitly describes AI-assisted coordination, while the current page describes operator target designation and engagement authorization. These are manufacturer claims, not independent testing. Confirmed exports and commercial-product scope at the HALCON producer level remain unresolved.

reviews.finding: The first delivery was 2 December 2025; 22 January 2026 was the announcement date. Official material describes operational use by 2026 without dating its start.
reviews.evidence_note: The DGA announcement dated 22 January 2026 reports delivery on 2 December 2025. Ministry material documents operational use by 2026 without establishing the first operational date. Recommend keeping receipt separate from fielding. Manufacturer specifications do not establish the configuration of a particular delivered batch. Delair also makes civil drones. No completed export, affirmative AI function or unit price was verified. Missing AI evidence is not evidence of exclusively traditional guidance. A daily production claim cannot establish measured annual output.

reviews.finding: German orders and trials are confirmed; operational fielding is not. The 5,400/year figure is an annualized July 2025 rate. The price is from a reported contract draft.
reviews.evidence_note: German orders and tests are documented; first operational fielding was not verified. The July 2025 report of 450 per month annualizes to 5,400 per year, but it is not measured annual production or verified 2026 capacity. Helsing separately advertises over 1,000 per month. A EUR 44,000 net draft-contract price converts to about USD 51,929 using 1.1802 USD/EUR on 26 February 2026; this is a reported estimate, not a confirmed paid price. Model-level AI and payload statements are manufacturer claims. The German delivery configuration was not verified. Commercial-product classification depends on whether and how subsidiary Grob is included.

reviews.finding: The current manufacturer page and September German-order interview give 75 minutes. An earlier announcement gave 90. Operational fielding remains unverified.
reviews.evidence_note: The German contract was announced on 26 February 2026; operational fielding was not verified. The manufacturer page checked in November and a September interview about the German order give 75 minutes, or 1.25 hours; the February release gave 90 minutes. The checked sources do not explain the difference as a version change. STARK explicitly describes onboard AI. A reported EUR 80,000 net estimate converts to USD 94,840 at 1.1855 USD/EUR on 16 February 2026; the contract draft price was redacted. Payload descriptions are advertised or tested options, not proof of the accepted German configuration.

reviews.finding: Latvian receipt is supported, but later warhead-integration reporting leaves operational fielding uncertain. AI is supported. “Beyond 10 km” is an engagement lower bound.
reviews.evidence_note: Latvian receipt was reported by February 2026. Later reporting about further warhead integration leaves the first operational date unresolved despite earlier delivery and deployment language. Origin explicitly describes AI computer vision. Engagement beyond 10 km is a lower bound, not an exact maximum flight distance. Earlier and later published warhead options do not identify Latvia’s delivered configuration. Unit price, annual capacity and a current commercial product line remain unverified. The founders’ previous Airdog business does not establish current Origin commercial production.

reviews.finding: Estonian receipt in January 2026 is supported. The sources describe evaluation and later testing, not completed operational fielding. Exact-model AI is supported.
reviews.evidence_note: Manufacturer-attributed reporting places first Estonian batches in January 2026. It describes evaluation and integration, and the Estonian Defence Forces reports March exercise testing. These establish receipt and testing, not first operational acceptance. Origin explicitly describes model-level AI-assisted recognition. Published range is an engagement lower bound. The fitted warhead, endurance and unit price of the delivered configuration remain unverified; small airframe mass does not establish price eligibility.

reviews.finding: FMV planned Raptor 2 delivery and handover for Q2 2027. The 45 km figure is a radio link. Generic RAPTOR AI and endurance claims do not settle the Swedish configuration.
reviews.evidence_note: FMV’s August 2026 announcement identifies Raptor 2 and plans delivery and military handover for Q2 2027. It does not establish Swedish receipt or fielding by the review date. The generic product page’s 45 km is radio-link range. Its three-hour endurance differs from a co-founder interview describing up to four hours for Raptor 2. Generic or developmental ML statements do not establish Sweden’s configuration. A mixed-system package cannot provide a unit cost without quantities and allocation. Historical mapping products do not settle current commercial-product classification.

reviews.finding: The 2024 order and July 2025 service-introduction statement are supported. First receipt and operational acceptance remain unresolved. The 2025 AI update is not linked to Australia’s order.
reviews.evidence_note: Australia announced a Switchblade 300 order in July 2024; contemporaneous reporting identifies Block 20. In July 2025 the government said service introduction was underway, without dating first receipt or completed operational acceptance. The current 30 km specification depends on an extended-range antenna. The later AI/EFP update is not established for the earlier Australian order. Quantix was discontinued, but current general commercial activity is documented. Related commercial UAS classification needs an explicit reference year. No supported unit price was found.

reviews.finding: The first shipment reached military warehouses in October 2026. That supports receipt, not an operational start date. The delivered block is unstated.
reviews.evidence_note: By the ministry’s 7 October 2026 announcement, the first Switchblade 600 shipment had reached Lithuanian military warehouses. The announcement does not establish the exact arrival day or operational start date. The delivered block is unstated, so newer Block 2 AI claims cannot be assumed. Procurement material’s target distance is not explicitly total flight range. The package includes equipment and support without a usable unit count. Current general commercial activity is documented; related commercial UAS classification needs a reference year. A producer statement of 240 systems per month in October 2025 annualizes to 2,880 per year, a historical rate rather than measured annual output or verified current capacity.
